answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards and randomly place number of players + 1 face-down on the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'one structure bonus tile'; 'The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'

answers.answer: Place each character at its home base; two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining the base; four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup pieces table and step 3: 'Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw'; 'Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards).'

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action (or either or both); bottom-first is forbidden and you cannot return to the top action after bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before acting; exposed green-box benefits are optional and may be taken as much or as little as desired. Exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must move the token'; 'First pay the full cost'; 'choose as much or as little ... benefit'; 'You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost.'

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources'; 'Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.'

answers.answer: On a normal unupgraded Move, select up to two different units for one adjacent territory each; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker's carried movement does not count as its own, so it may subsequently move itself, or may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move. All units (characters, mechs, workers) carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move: 'two different units, one adjacent territory each'; 'Being carried does not count as the worker's own movement'; 'Only mechs may also carry ... your workers, never your character.'

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech stops and cannot move again that turn when it enters a territory occupied only by enemy workers; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero. Having zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops'; 'workers immediately retreat'; 'insufficient popularity does not prevent the retreat'; workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve all combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order'; workers cannot independently move 'into or out of' territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades; traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster: '$1, gain two power OR one combat card'; 'If both are empty, draw none.' Trade: '$1'; resources on 'a controlled territory containing at least one worker'; 'cannot Trade ... if all your workers are at home.'

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production, then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades. Each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the current cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps: 'Pay every exposed Produce cost ... in full before production'; 'Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right'; 'You may decline some or all production'; new costs affect 'future Produce actions.'

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Upgrade — oil; Deploy — metal; placement on 'a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake'; 'Even after completing all ... you may still pay for that bottom action.'

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A controlled Mill grants its bonus Produce territory and production; an enemy unit on its territory means you do not control it, so Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. A Mine remains your personal tunnel for movement to and from it even while enemies occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions.
answers.evidence: Build: 'controlled territory with your worker'; structures 'cannot be moved or destroyed'; Mill bonus applies 'only while controlled'; Mine allows movement 'even when enemy-controlled.'

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where you removed the recruit, not the one-time choice. When you or either immediate neighbor takes the matching bottom action, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: 'put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus'; ongoing bonus is the circle 'where you removed the recruit'; resolve 'active player first, then left, then right'; two-player opponent triggers once.

answers.answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly selects dial power from 0 up to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army permits one additional card total if any workers are present). If both players have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Both deduct selected dial power from their Power Tracks and discard every played card face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4: 'simultaneously and secretly choose'; 'Reveal simultaneously'; 'attacker wins ties'; both deduct dial power and discard cards face-up.

answers.answer: Winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources; Nordic Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6 specify retreat of 'all characters, mechs and workers,' resources left, attacker popularity loss, defender none, and losing-player card condition.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains in the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All gained resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and gain no additional mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: 'after the whole Move action and all combats'; if entry is lost, 'the token stays'; gains go to 'the encounter territory'; 'no additional normal action costs' or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character takes one Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if necessary; each chooses one from the available cards and returns the rest. Each player may have at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); similar Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a Speed-enabled character/mech, with normal restrictions (including Mine access and movement stops).
answers.evidence: Factory: 'Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action there'; 'one permanent card'; fifth action section; bottom action moves one unit up to two, or three with Speed.

answers.answer: Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives: 'Only on your own turn'; 'meet all requirements at the moment of reveal'; put 'both objective cards on the bottom'; Saxony 'can score both.'

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars, Saxony unrestricted within six), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception; other players' stars do not block it. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops. The sixth star ends play immediately.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all goals; 'Other players’ stars never block a goal'; 'A placed star is permanent'; 'sixth star immediately ends play.'

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement part and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor recruit bonuses/stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor in order, checking for the sixth star each time; after an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence: collect 'primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing'; undo unresolved battle movement; neighbor sequence and stop condition stated.

answers.answer: At popularity 10, use the 7–12 tier: each of 5 stars adds $4 ($20 total); 4 normal territories plus Factory count as 4 + 3 = 7 scoring territories at $3 each ($21); 13 resources make 6 complete pairs at $2 each ($12). Thus those categories add $53 to held coins, before the selected structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures. Victory tiebreakers are workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Scoring table gives 7–12 values ($4, $3, $2); Factory counts as 3; resource pairs round down; structure bonus earned despite enemy control; tiebreak order listed.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control section: 'A home base is not a territory'; default no entry/build/deploy, with listed exceptions; unmatched bases are inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, villages workers; lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; 'workers are not resources'; 'Resource tokens have no supply limit: use multipliers if needed.'

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; mechs may also pick up/carry/drop your workers, but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step and the extra step may be before or after it; mechs can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: all units carry resources; mechs carry workers but not character; Speed and tunnel step details and stop overrides stated.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure'; 'All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.'

answers.answer: You never pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, a legal dead turn is to move the token to a different section and take neither action; thus after last using Move, choose a different section and skip both actions if necessary.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn by moving the token to a different section and taking neither action. Never pay only part of a cost.'

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These apply to the matching future action and the owner keeps the structure ability even without control, unless an uncontrolled Mill (the exception) is involved; an enemy occupant does not gain the building's ability.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade specify Monument and Armory bonuses; control section says you keep abilities without control and enemies do not gain them.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is for characters and mechs: Rusviet to farms/villages; Crimea to farms/tundra; Nordic to forests/mountains; Polania to villages/mountains; Saxony to forests/mountains. Nordic Swim instead lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction ability table lists Riverwalk destinations for character/mechs; Nordic Swim says workers alone, not lakes, and not character/mechs.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions each specify 'character/mech Move actions.'

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine, making the opponent lose two power on the track, once per combat rather than per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets you pay one power before combat to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat rather than per unit.
answers.evidence: Disarm and Artillery descriptions give timing, location/cost, effect, and once-per-combat frequency.

answers.answer: With two mechs and three workers in the combat, Rusviet People's Army allows one additional combat card total beyond the usual one per participating character/mech; the summary's example says two mechs and three workers allow three cards. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: People's Army: 'one additional combat card total'; 'Two mechs and three workers allow three cards'; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own home base or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Wayfare: move to 'your own or any inactive faction home base'; 'not an active opponent's base.'

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random combat card from the opponent into your hand before combat, once per combat and not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.
answers.evidence: Scout: 'steal one random opponent combat card into your hand'; Coercion: spend one card as any one resource, regardless of value.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and permits retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but grants no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Seaworthy and Submerge descriptions distinguish lake movement/retreat; lake rule states workers need a mech and carriers cannot leave workers/resources behind.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not cover popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie: no loss 'after you win combat as aggressor on your turn'; 'does not protect' against loss for undefended workers without combat.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second option's cost. Pay the printed cost for each selected option, and may take as little of each benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Meander: 'up to two different options ... in either order; first gain can pay second cost'; encounter options allow taking as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter-token territory during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounter rules apply 'during Factory Move'; character stops; encounter is after whole Move action and all combats.

answers.answer: Combat-card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal whether you committed any combat cards until reveal; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until a completed objective is revealed. Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total value when asked.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table states these rules for combat cards, objectives, and coins.

answers.answer: Players may make informal, unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat follows Move, though bribes may still influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: agreements are 'unenforceable'; 'Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable'; negotiation cannot cancel initiated combat.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory counted, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per resource pair. Popularity 13–18: $5 per star, $4 per territory, $3 per resource pair. Controlled lakes count and home bases do not. Pool resources across controlled territories and ignore an odd leftover token.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table and accompanying rules: controlled lakes count, home bases do not, and resource pairs round down.

answers.answer: For adjacency tiles, each feature is unique across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent tunnel features are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; adjacent encounter locations count even if their token is removed; adjacent lakes are unique lakes. Payouts for each adjacency category are 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; tunnels 6 $9, lakes/encounters 6–7 $9. Zero qualifying features score zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table: unique features, tunnels not Mines, removed encounter still counts, payouts; rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 gives $2, 2 gives $4, 3–4 gives $6. Structures in a row score only the longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras count combined qualifying structures: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table entries for structures on tunnels, in a row, and on farms/tundras; row note says rivers do not break the line.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated combat exception.
answers.evidence: Combat: winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, 'even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.'

answers.answer: No. A placed popularity star is permanent even if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines the final scoring tier. Another player's star never blocks your goal, so two factions can each earn a star for the same achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars: permanent even if popularity drops; current popularity determines final scoring; other players' stars never block a goal.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses trigger for you and your immediate left and right neighbors.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–3 deal mats and list faction order; Ongoing recruits defines immediate left/right neighbor triggers.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability can enter the lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move: 'A river is a border between two land territories'; lake definition and entry from 'any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.'

answers.answer: No, you cannot keep the drawn encounter card private. Show the card to all players, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: 'Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud'; options need not all be read.

answers.answer: There is no limit to the number of friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.'

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin 'while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.'

answers.answer: No. Each selected section's top action and bottom action may each be taken at most once that turn; the token must move to a different section next turn. Rusviet may repeat a section across turns, including its Factory card, but the summary does not allow repeating the same action in the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says take that section's top action once and bottom action once; must move token; Rusviet may repeat a section.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal Move top action.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: 'Alternatively gain $1.'

answers.answer: No. The summary says workers never return to the Player Mat; workers forced to retreat go to their home base, so they cannot be returned to the mat to cover Produce costs again.
answers.evidence: Produce: 'Workers never return to the Player Mat'; forced retreat is to the worker's home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both; combat dial power may be selected as zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: 'You may attack with zero power/popularity'; dial range begins at 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary non-Saxony limit is two combat stars.
answers.evidence: Combat: 'You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit'; ordinary maximum two.

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option; it cannot decline to choose. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. It must pay the printed cost, but may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: without Meander, 'must choose one affordable option'; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected; benefit may be partial.

answers.answer: No. Both combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, then reveal simultaneously; selected combat cards are also revealed at that reveal, rather than in turn order.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: combatants 'simultaneously and secretly choose' and 'Reveal simultaneously.'

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses; the active player and then eligible immediate neighbors may receive the corresponding exposed ongoing bonus.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: 'Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses'; ongoing bonuses trigger when neighbors take corresponding action.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as its achievement is reached, and the sixth star immediately ends the game. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but when revealing you must meet all requirements at that moment and it must be on your own turn at the permitted time.
answers.evidence: Stars: 'Place a star as soon as you achieve'; sixth star immediately ends; objective section says 'You may wait' to reveal.

answers.answer: Normally, characters, mechs, and workers cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide the exceptions.'

answers.answer: No. The recruit is put permanently on an open one-time recruit bonus on the Faction Mat and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit put 'permanently' on the space; 'It cannot later move.'

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering that territory does not resolve the encounter or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: 'Only a character triggers an encounter.'

answers.answer: While controlled, a Mill provides one bonus production territory in addition to the normal territories selected, so two normal territories permit up to three with a Mill (or an upgraded allowance of three permits up to four). The Mill itself counts as one producing worker, and each actual worker there also produces normally. The Mill can produce on its terrain even with no actual worker present.
answers.evidence: Produce: Mill bonus added to current allowance; 'Mill itself counts as one producing worker'; 'each actual worker there may also produce normally'; Mill may produce without actual worker.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. If your last unit leaves a territory with no structure of yours, resources alone do not maintain your control; resources are not listed as establishing control.
answers.evidence: Control definition: control is by 'a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit'; resources are not listed as a control condition.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions list: 'Build — wood; Enlist — food.'
